text:
Every SSD stores data in NAND flash cells. Most drives use TLC (triple-level cell) flash, and each TLC cell lasts roughly 3,000 write cycles before it starts to wear out. That sounds low, but drives have two ways of dealing with it.

The first is wear leveling. The controller spreads writes evenly across all the blocks, so no single cell takes most of the writes while the cells next to it sit unused.

The second is over-provisioning. Drives keep a reserve of spare flash, usually about 7%, that you can't see. The controller uses it to replace worn-out blocks and keep performance steady.

With both of these, those 3,000 cycles last for years of normal use, whether you're storing photos, games or work files.
